chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid al-Qummi, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, used to say:

"O son of Adam! You will always be in a good state as long as you have an admonisher from within yourself, and as long as self-reckoning is among your concerns, and as long as fear is your inner garment and sorrow is your outer garment.
O son of Adam! Indeed, you will die and be resurrected and made to stand before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and be questioned. So prepare an answer."

key_terms.المحاسبة: Self-reckoning; the practice of holding oneself accountable for deeds.
key_terms.دثار: Outer garment or cloak; metaphor for something that envelops and is always visible.
key_terms.شعار: Inner garment worn next to the skin; metaphor for something deeply internalized.
key_terms.مبعوث: Resurrected; raised from the dead on the Day of Judgment.
key_terms.واعظ: An admonisher; one who gives counsel and warning. Here used metaphorically for the inner conscience.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about self-accountability and preparing for the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the fourth Imam and grandson of Imam Husayn (AS), delivered this exhortation through his close companion Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He addresses humankind as "son of Adam" -- a Quranic trope used when delivering universal moral reminders. The Imam emphasizes that spiritual well-being depends on four internal states: self-admonition, rigorous self-accounting, fear of God as a constant inner disposition, and sorrow over one's shortcomings. He then reminds the listener of the certainty of death, resurrection, and divine interrogation, urging preparation of an answer for the Day of Judgment.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
